source.section: PA-40 lines 1a to 12 (form pages 1-2); PDF page 1 and form line 12 rate 3.07 percent; PDF page 9 no standard deduction or exemptions; PDF page 20 Lines 9 and 10; PDF page 21 Lines 11 and 12; PDF page 15 'Annuities, Life Insurance, or Endowment Contracts'; PDF page 13 Code 7 CAUTION; PDF page 31 Schedule A; projection: all annuities are taxed

worked: Commercial annuity at 68, bought outside any employer plan: interest income to the extent federally taxable, as the projection taxes every annuity. Federal AGI = annuity person 0 20,000.00 + interest 5,000.00 = 25,000.00. Federal taxable income = 25,000.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 + age 65 addition 2,000.00 = 7,250.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Pennsylvania, as the projection works it: start federal AGI 25,000.00; annuity 20,000.00 stays taxed (no relief covers it); income after reliefs = 25,000.00. No standard deduction or exemption (PDF page 9), no Line 10 deduction: state taxable income 25,000.00. Tax = 25,000.00 x 0.0307 = 767.50. No credit in the projection; state income tax 767.50. Form: Line 1a/1c 0.00; Line 2 25,000.00; Line 3 0.00; Line 5 0.00; Line 9 25,000.00; Line 10 0.00; Line 11 25,000.00; Line 12 767.50 (the form, in whole dollars, PDF page 4, shows 768). Schedule SP: Eligibility Income 25,000.00 is over 8,750.00, so no Tax Forgiveness on the form either.
accepted_approximations: Pennsylvania has no federal starting point: it adds the positive amounts of eight classes (compensation, interest, dividends, business, gains, rents, estates and trusts, gambling). The mapping runs from federal AGI to those classes: start from federal AGI, then take out what the reliefs below exempt. Wages, interest, dividends, gains, business income and rents are taken as federal AGI holds them, in one sum. The differences that remain are listed one by one in the next four entries.
All annuities are taxed; one from an eligible employer plan after retirement is exempt (not_modelled entry). A commercial annuity is taxed as the projection does.
